name: 01-erdos-renyi-random-growth
title: Erdős–Rényi random growth
question: What topology emerges when edges form purely at random, with no preference?
hypothesis: Random attachment yields a homogeneous Poisson degree distribution with no hubs — the null baseline for every structured rule that follows.
objective: Run the erdos_renyi reaction and show how it reconfigures the network, measuring its signature structural observables.
description:
Random growth produces a homogeneous, hub-free network (Poisson-like degrees) — the null baseline the structured rules are read against.

The network is stored as process-bigraph node/edge maps and reconfigured each step by the `erdos_renyi` reaction (emitting _add/_remove structural sentinels). The animation and GIF in viz/ show the evolution; scalar metrics are emitted for the behavior tests.
claim: Random growth produces a homogeneous, hub-free network (Poisson-like degrees) — the null baseline the structured rules are read against.

config.title: Erdős–Rényi random growth
config.subtitle: node arrives each step, links to each existing node w.p. p

expected_behavior.name: er-no-hubs
expected_behavior.condition: max degree stays close to the mean (no heavy tail)
expected_behavior.rationale: Uniform random attachment gives Poisson degrees; the maximum is only modestly above the mean.

expected_behavior.name: er-connects
expected_behavior.condition: a giant component spans almost all nodes by the end
expected_behavior.rationale: Above the percolation threshold ⟨k⟩>1 a giant component emerges (Erdős–Rényi).

behavior_tests.name: er-giant-component
behavior_tests.description: A giant component spans ≥90% of nodes at the end.

behavior_tests.name: er-no-dominant-hub
behavior_tests.description: Max degree is modest (< 4× mean degree) — no scale-free hub.

findings.name: erdos_renyi-signature
findings.summary: Random growth produces a homogeneous, hub-free network (Poisson-like degrees) — the null baseline the structured rules are read against.
findings.detail: Random growth gives a connected but hub-free graph; the degree spread is narrow, establishing the null against which preferential attachment's hubs stand out.
